reading.source_scope_note: Randomized two-group online vignette experiment with psychology students reading20 hypothetical self-driving-car incident headlines and rating trust plus free-text blame. Recruited283; reported usable192 conflicts with a Welch test’s274.66df if that test uses one independent participant mean. Aggregate wording contrast is nonsignificant; two of20 headline tests have unadjustedp.03/.01. Descriptive word frequencies do not establish blame intensity, legal liability, actual cyberattacks, trust decline or an AI mental state.
access_limits: All16 supplied postprint pages read, including image-only table and all figures. Public ORCA PDFhttps://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/160610/1/Marcinkiewicz.%20Trust%20and%20blame%20in%20self-driving.pdf matches exactly. Final typeset conference article is subscription content and was not read or purchased.

No accessible raw dataset, analysis code, registration, supplement containing all20 headline pairs, exact group sizes, missingness by condition or complete lexical coding rules was identified on the inspected publisher/repository pages. No author contact, participant reidentification or raw-data replication.

The paper reports a closing cyber-term familiarity measure but explicitly does not report its data. Initial general trust/adoption questions are described without reported pre/post change; no baseline-adjusted trust decrease is recoverable.

Primary NIST glossary targeted definition verified, not the fullSP800-152. SAE level distinctions were checked against the primary SAE2021 chart reproduced in the supplied PDF; fullJ3016 and current road law were not read. No current legal driving advice is provided.

Crossref verifies selected reference identities only: Sheehan2019, Pham/Xiong2021 and Holthausen et al.2020. Those originals and Cohen1972’s full book were not read. No independent experimental or book-reading credit is added for them.
No real vehicle/attack test, physiological measurement, new survey, full-paper Markdown archive, extra page or invented annual mention count.

study.sample: 283 Cardiff psychology students, age18–36, mean19.90(SD2.20); later usableN192 after completeness screening, a91-person/32.2% difference. Group assignment and headline order randomized. This is a convenience student sample, not a general driver population or actual autonomous-vehicle users. Actual retained group counts are not given.
study.materials: 20 pairs of hypothetical news headlines adapted from news, each with identical20–30-word subtext within a pair. Overt-cyber wording includes hackers/attackers/cyber, covert wording substitutes non-specific descriptions. Each participant receives one wording condition across20 incidents, not both versions of each pair. Only examples and selected contrasts are supplied, not all paired stimuli.
study.measures: A single100-point visual analogue slider per headline for trust, followed by open-ended blame. Slider numbers hidden from participants. This is a bespoke self-report, not a validatedSTS-AD administration, observed reliance or actual safety measure. Hiding a numeric label may reduce rounding cues but cannot guarantee absence of repetition, response bias or demand effects.
study.missingness: 43 missing trust ratings are mentioned, with person-mean substitution when at most2of20 are missing and exclusion otherwise. Person-mean imputation may shrink within-person variation and assumes missingness is sufficiently benign. The exact analysis sample for each test, sensitivity analyses and whether the reported192 applies to all analyses are not recoverable.
study.trust_results: All headline means reportedly below50/100. Overall between-condition WilcoxonW10573,p.42 and transformed Welch t.372,df274.66,p.71 are nonsignificant. Low post-headline ratings are not an observed decline without reported baseline/no-incident comparison. Lack of significance is not equivalence or proof that wording never affects trust.
study.statistical_reporting: The source calls an independent-group comparison a Wilcoxon-Rank sign test; signed-rank and rank-sum tests differ. Test label/statistic convention cannot be recovered without output. A standard two-sample Welchdf cannot exceedN−2:274.66 is incompatible with one independent mean for each of192participants, whose maximumdf is190. It requires at least277independent observations under that model. Larger originalN283 could accommodate it, but does not prove whichN or procedure was actually used.
study.normality: A Shapiro-Wilk result is labeledS.0007958 withp<.05. This may be a mislabeledp-value rather than theWstatistic. A normality test rejects normality, not specifically establishes direction of skew; a histogram supplies the reported directional indication. No inventedWor originalp-value.
study.headline_tests: Two of20 between-condition headline contrasts have reportedp.03 andp.01; none of those two meets simpleBonferroni.05/20=.0025. No multiplicity correction or fullp-vector is supplied. The authors expressly call these ambiguous exploratory signals and urge caution; do not portray them as two independently confirmed mechanisms.
study.severity_and_intent: Selected within-condition comparisons reportW4465,p2.2e−16 for severity andW8454,p.03 for malicious/accidental cause. Headlines can differ on more than one feature, and the authors explicitly limit these isolated scenarios and defer further studies. Do not infer a clean factorial causal severity/intent mechanism or new moral doctrine.
study.blame: Image-onlyTable1 lists left/right paired frequencies: company493/489; manufacturer380 versus hackers421; vehicle301 versus attackers269; employee200 versus vehicle223; internet88 versus security197. Column headers both sayCC, although text intendsCCandOC comparison. Top-five sums1462+1599=3061 match the caption’s frequency figure. These are mentions, not unique participants or mutually exclusive blame shares.
study.coding: Spelling corrections and partial synonym normalization are described, but company/manufacturer and attackers/hackers remain distinct lexical terms. Multiple entities can be blamed per response. Coding reliability, complete denominator, condition-specific response totals and inferential blame comparison are not supplied. Word clouds show lexical frequency, not causal responsibility, blame intensity or legal liability.
study.causal_scope: Between-condition wording assignment supports a local experimental contrast, subject to missingness and reporting uncertainty. Overt terms also communicate potentially relevant causal/agent information, so lexical differences are not automatically irrational framing or a generic priming effect. No actual attack or driver behavior was observed.
study.limits_acknowledged: The authors describe bespoke scale limitations, hypothetical/online context, ambiguity of the two headline results, unknown relative blame weighting and need for future physiological/interface studies. Preserve these qualifications rather than allege all weaknesses were hidden.
study.ethics: Informed-consent and withdrawal procedures plus CardiffSREC approval/risk assessment are explicitly reported. Do not infer absent ethics review. Future eye tracking and interface-based trust restoration are proposals, not completed evidence or direct readouts of deep semantic processing.

summary: No new ontology row. Enrich existing blame attribution, performance trust and framing with a fully read conference experiment, retaining its null aggregate wording contrast and descriptive lexical results. Add non-counted context for trust damage/repair. Verify metadata and reporting discrepancies without inventing corrected samples, effects, blame shares or real-world safety conclusions.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.

evidence.quote: the SDC company was blamed the most

findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers this mechanism. Distinguish hypothetical perceptions, wording, realized conduct and objective safety rather than adding a new context-specific duplicate.
findings.evidence_scope: Free-text responses after20 hypothetical incidents most frequently name the vehicle company; overt-cyber wording produces more hacker/attacker terms. Multiple entities may be named. This is a descriptive lexical attribution result without a reported inferential blame test.
findings.boundary: Mention frequency does not measure intensity, causal responsibility or legal liability. Company/manufacturer and hacker/attacker labels may overlap semantically; denominators and coding reliability are not fully supplied. Multiple blame targets are not evidence of diffusion or complete displacement of human responsibility.

findings.definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.

evidence.quote: to what extent participants’ trust an SDC based on each news headline

findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers this mechanism. Distinguish hypothetical perceptions, wording, realized conduct and objective safety rather than adding a new context-specific duplicate.
findings.evidence_scope: Single-slider perceived trust in a hypothetical driving system after a reported incident; all headline means below50/100 and no significant aggregate overt/covert wording difference. The source treats trust as relevant to acceptance but does not measure actual reliance.
findings.boundary: Low stated trust is not evidence of actual system unreliability, a measured trust decrease, avoidance behavior or an AI feeling. A bespoke self-report and missing baseline results cannot establish safe adoption; uncertainty and sample/test discrepancies remain visible.

findings.definition: Differences in judgment or choice under alternative presentations of otherwise equivalent information.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers this mechanism. Distinguish hypothetical perceptions, wording, realized conduct and objective safety rather than adding a new context-specific duplicate.
findings.evidence_scope: Randomized overt-cyber versus non-specific news wording has a nonsignificant overall trust contrast. Two unadjusted headline differences are exploratory; lexical blame categories vary with wording.
findings.boundary: This is boundary evidence, not a replicated broad framing effect. Words such as hackers can provide relevant causal information, and nonsignificance does not prove equivalence. Do not promote20 exploratory comparisons into independent discoveries or label every appropriate information update a bias.

findings.definition: A reduction in trust following a failure, which can remain after that failure is reported corrected.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers this mechanism. Distinguish hypothetical perceptions, wording, realized conduct and objective safety rather than adding a new context-specific duplicate.
findings.evidence_scope: Incident-related erosion is the research motivation, and ratings after adverse hypothetical headlines are low. The described initial trust question is not accompanied by a reported within-person decline or a no-incident control contrast.
findings.boundary: Context only: low post-incident trust is not a demonstrated loss from baseline. The experiment compares two adverse wording conditions, not harm versus no harm. Keep future trust-loss hypotheses separate from an observed longitudinal deterioration.

findings.definition: Actions intended to restore trust after a failure, violation or disagreement has damaged it.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers this mechanism. Distinguish hypothetical perceptions, wording, realized conduct and objective safety rather than adding a new context-specific duplicate.
findings.evidence_scope: Discussion proposes informative interfaces and safe responses as potential supports after adverse incidents.
findings.boundary: Context only: no repair intervention, recovery trajectory or subsequent reliance was tested. Restoration should depend on repaired trustworthiness and adequate evidence, rather than increasing confidence for commercial adoption alone.

methodological_limits: Hypothetical headlines and a convenience psychology-student sample do not establish behavior during an actual attack, actual vehicle safety, legal blame or deployment adoption.
No significant aggregate contrast is not an equivalence result. Low trust after adverse reports is not a demonstrated decline from baseline.
Missingness and unclear sample/test reporting constrain inference. Person-mean substitution may alter variability; raw output and sensitivity checks are unavailable.
Open-ended lexical frequencies are descriptive, may repeat people and overlapping actor labels, and provide no blame weighting or legal allocation.
Overt wording changes causal/agent information as well as phrasing. An appropriate update from informative words is not automatically bias or priming.
VAS granularity does not guarantee validity; eye movements or physiological arousal do not directly read trust or deep semantic processing. Proposed measures and interfaces were not tested.
Authors openly acknowledge hypothetical context, bespoke scale, ambiguous headline signals and missing blame weighting. Preserve those cautions.
No new concept, category, principle, automatic harm link, forced citation quota, invented annual total or extra page.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The primary NISTglossary includes the quoted definition underSP800-152. It is not a fabricated quotation. Its system-property context still differs from a validated measure of human subjective trust.
The two top-five mention sums1462and1599add to3061. Lexical counts are distinct from the283recruited or192reportedusable people; multiple/repeated attributions are possible.
The paper reports a null aggregate result, cautions about the two headline signals, describes bespoke-scale limitations and says blame weights were not obtained.
Consent and withdrawal procedures are explicit, and an ethics/risk-assessment statement namesCardiffSREC.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Signed-rank and rank-sum ambiguity proves allWvalues impossible
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: DifferentWstatistic conventions exist, and within-person severity comparisons differ from between-condition wording comparisons. The label requires clarification; numbers are not corrected from assumptions alone.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Repeated ratings and unit mismatches require explicit denominators. Perception and attribution do not by themselves establish responsibility transfer or actual capacity.
Nonsignificant wording/transparency effects do not establish universal failure or remove oversight value. Retain narrower treatment scope and explicit author limitations.
